definition_zh: 学位论文；论点；论题；命题
definition_en: a long research essay submitted for a university degree, or a proposition put forward for argument
core_image: 一叠装订好的论文放在答辩桌上，封面印着标题与作者名
scene: 答辩室里，学生把装订好的论文递给评审，然后开始陈述自己的核心论点。In the defence room, the student handed the bound thesis to the examiners and then stated the central claim.
sceneCN: 这里 thesis 是「学位论文」（第 1 个义项：为取得学位而提交的研究长文）；句意：答辩室里，学生把装订好的论文递给评审，然后陈述核心论点。

derivatives.zh: 对立面；反题，由 anti-（相反）加 thesis 构成
假设；假说，由 hypo-（在下）加 thesis 构成，字面义为「放在下面的命题」
正题的；直陈的，由 thesis 加 -tic 构成

senses.title: A degree dissertation
senses.definition: a long piece of writing based on research, submitted for a university degree
senses.definitionCN: 基于研究写成、为取得大学学位而提交的长篇论文
senses.example: She spent two years collecting data for her doctoral thesis.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了两年时间为博士论文收集数据。
senses.why: The Greek word for a placing became the written work that a candidate lays before examiners.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语中「放置」这个词，变成了候选人摆到评审面前的那部长篇作品。

senses.title: The central claim
senses.definition: the main claim that an essay or a talk sets out to prove
senses.definitionCN: 文章或演讲试图证明的核心主张
senses.example: The thesis of the article is that remote work changes office life.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章的中心论点是远程工作改变了办公室生活。
senses.why: A thesis is a proposition laid down, so it also names the claim a writer places at the centre.
senses.whyCN: thesis 本是被放下的命题，因此也指作者摆到文章中心的那条主张。

senses.title: A proposition for argument
senses.definition: a statement put forward for discussion and proof
senses.definitionCN: 提出来供讨论并加以证明的陈述
senses.example: The debate class tested each thesis with evidence and counterexamples.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论课用证据和反例逐一检验每个命题。
senses.why: Logic kept the original sense of a proposition placed for argument.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学保留了原义：一条被摆出来、等待论证的命题。

senses.title: The first term in dialectic
senses.definition: the first proposition in a dialectical pattern, which is answered by an antithesis
senses.definitionCN: 辩证模式中的第一个命题，由反题来回应
senses.example: In the Hegelian pattern, the thesis is met by an antithesis and resolved in a synthesis.
senses.exampleCN: 在黑格尔式模式中，正题遭遇反题，并在合题中得到解决。
senses.why: Philosophy used the placing image for the first term that is set down before its opposite.
senses.whyCN: 哲学用「放置」的意象指先被放下、随后遭遇对立面的第一个命题。

senses.title: A stressed beat in music
senses.definition: the strong beat of a bar, on which the movement of a phrase lands
senses.definitionCN: 小节中的强拍，乐句的运动在此落定
senses.example: The conductor marked the thesis with a firm downward stroke.
senses.exampleCN: 指挥用一个有力的下压动作标出强拍。
senses.why: Greek metrics called the placing of the foot on the beat a thesis, and music kept the downbeat image.
senses.whyCN: 希腊韵律学把脚落在拍点上称为 thesis，音乐则保留了这个「落拍」意象。

intro.en: Thesis comes from Greek thesis, a placing or a proposition, from tithenai, to place or put.
intro.cn: thesis 来自希腊语 thesis（放置、命题），源于 tithenai（放置、安放）。

items.en: Tithenai means to place or to put something down.
items.cn: tithenai 意为放置、把某物放下。

items.en: Thesis means a placing, and then a proposition laid down.
items.cn: thesis 意为放置，进而指被放下的命题。

items.en: Latin borrows thesis for a proposition and for a stressed beat.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 thesis，用来指命题与强拍。

items.en: English thesis first names a proposition in logic and learning.
items.cn: 英语 thesis 最早指逻辑与学术中的命题。

items.en: The word extends to a subject laid out for formal debate.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到为正式辩论而摆出的论题。

items.en: Thesis becomes the long research essay submitted for a degree.
items.cn: 现代英语中，thesis 指为取得学位而提交的研究长文。

note.en: Thesis is the Greek placing word behind antithesis and hypothesis, and it sits near dissertation, essay, and argument.
note.cn: thesis 是希腊语「放置」词，构成 antithesis 与 hypothesis，并与 dissertation、essay、argument 意义相邻。

entries.definition: the opposite proposition in a dialectical pair
entries.definitionCN: 辩证配对中的反题；对立面

entries.definition: a supposition put forward as a starting point
entries.definitionCN: 作为出发点提出的假设

entries.definition: positive, laid down directly
a long research essay written for a degree
entries.definitionCN: 为取得学位而写的长篇研究论文，与 thesis 的论文义接近

entries.definition: a short piece of writing on a subject
entries.definitionCN: 短文；随笔，篇幅通常比 thesis 短

entries.definition: a set of reasons offered for a claim
entries.definitionCN: 论证；说理，对应 thesis 的论点义

normalIntro.en: Thesis comes from Greek tithenai, to place, so a thesis is a claim placed before readers.
normalIntro.cn: thesis 来自希腊语 tithenai（放置），所以论文与论点都是摆到读者面前的东西。

normal.en: Thesis and tithenai share the Greek image of placing something down.
normal.cn: thesis 与 tithenai 共享希腊语「把东西放下」的意象。

normal.en: A doctoral thesis is the long work a candidate places before examiners.
normal.cn: 博士论文是候选人摆到评审面前的长篇作品。

normal.en: The thesis statement tells the reader what the essay will prove.
normal.cn: 论点陈述告诉读者这篇文章要证明什么。

normal.en: To defend a thesis is to answer the questions of the examiners.
normal.cn: 进行论文答辩，就是回答评审提出的问题。

normal.en: Compare dissertation: dissertation is the book, thesis can also be the claim.
normal.cn: 对比 dissertation：dissertation 指那本书，thesis 还可以指书中的主张。

abstract.en: Picture a bound volume placed on a defence table.
abstract.cn: 想象一本装订好的论文放在答辩桌上。

abstract.en: Picture one sentence underlined at the top of a page.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸的顶端有一句话被画了下划线。

abstract.en: Picture a stone marker set down on a debate table.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石制标记被放在辩论桌上。

examples.en: Her thesis examines how students learn to write academic English.
examples.cn: 她的论文研究学生如何学习学术英语写作。

examples.en: The supervisor asked him to state the thesis in one sentence.
examples.cn: 导师让他用一句话说清中心论点。

examples.en: Several theses in the library cover the same period of history.
examples.cn: 图书馆里有好几篇论文研究同一段历史。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「西塞斯」——西施把论文塞进书桌；谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 希腊语 tithenai（放置）→ thesis（放置；被放下的命题）→ 拉丁语 thesis → 英语 thesis，核心义「把主张摆出来、放下」。

sensesIntro.en: Thesis moves from the act of placing to the claim placed before readers, then to the degree essay, the dialectical first term, and the musical downbeat.
sensesIntro.cn: thesis 从「放置」这一动作，转到摆到读者面前的论点，再引申为学位论文、辩证法正题与音乐强拍。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bound dissertation laid on the table of a defence room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本装订好的论文放在答辩室的桌上。

branches.en: The degree dissertation is the main academic sense.
branches.cn: 学位论文是主要的学术义项。

branches.en: The central claim is the essay sense.
branches.cn: 中心论点是文章层面的义项。

branches.en: The proposition for argument is the logical sense.
branches.cn: 待论证命题是逻辑义项。

branches.en: The dialectical first term is the philosophical sense.
branches.cn: 辩证法正题是哲学义项。

branches.en: The stressed beat is the musical sense.
branches.cn: 强拍是音乐义项。

intro.en: Thesis is built on Greek tithenai, to place, with the action-noun ending -sis; antithesis and hypothesis are the same root with different prefixes.
intro.cn: thesis 建在希腊语 tithenai（放置）之上，动作名词词尾 -sis 使其成为「放置」这一行为；antithesis 与 hypothesis 则是换用不同前缀的同根词。

latinIntro.en: Greek tithenai means to place, thesis means a placing or proposition, and Latin borrowed thesis with both senses.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 tithenai 意为放置，thesis 意为放置或命题，拉丁语把这两个含义一并借入。

items.example: Tithenai is the verb behind thesis.
items.exampleCN: tithenai 是 thesis 背后的动词。

items.example: Greek thesis joins the placing action with a claim.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 thesis 把放置动作与主张连在一起。

items.example: Latin thesis keeps the proposition and the beat.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 thesis 保留命题与强拍两个含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的名词词尾
items.example: The ending -sis turns a verb of placing into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -sis 把「放置」动词变成名词。

items.meaning: a placing against, the opposite proposition
items.example: Antithesis sets a second claim against the first.
items.exampleCN: antithesis 把第二个主张放到第一个的对面。

items.example: Hypothesis places a starting claim under an inquiry.
items.exampleCN: hypothesis 把一个起点主张放在探究之下。

items.example: Synthesis places the two sides together.
Parenthesis places extra words beside the main line.
items.exampleCN: parenthesis 把额外的词放在主线旁边。

items.example: Thetic describes a claim laid down without opposition.
items.exampleCN: thetic 描述未经对立就直接放下的主张。

items.meaning: a degree essay or a claim
items.example: English thesis keeps the essay and the claim.
items.exampleCN: 英语 thesis 同时保留论文与论点两个含义。

definition_zh: 渴的；口干的；渴望的；干旱的
definition_en: feeling a need to drink, or wanting something very much
core_image: 喉咙里像塞了一把干沙：整个身体在喊水
scene: 足球赛下半场,他扶着膝盖大口喘气。The thirsty players lined up at the water table after the match.
sceneCN: 这里 thirsty 是「口渴的」（第 1 个义项：身体需要喝水）；句意：赛后口渴的球员们在饮水台前排起了队。

pos.zh: 渴望的；饥渴的（与 for 连用）

collocations.zh: 使人口渴的活儿；累人的事

derivatives.zh: 渴；口渴；渴望（thirsty 的名词基础）
口渴地；急切地（thirsty 加副词后缀 -ly）
嗜血的；残忍的（blood 加 thirsty 构成的复合词）
解渴；平息（与 thirst 搭配的动词，非同根）

senses.title: Needing to drink
senses.definition: feeling the need or wish to drink water
senses.definitionCN: 感到需要或想喝水
senses.example: The long climb left everyone thirsty.
senses.exampleCN: 长途攀登让每个人都渴了。
senses.why: The body speaks through the throat: dryness there is the whole message, and thirsty is its word.
senses.whyCN: 身体借喉咙发言：那里的干涩就是全部讯息，thirsty 便是这讯息的词。

senses.title: Strongly wanting something
senses.definition: having a strong desire for something, usually with for
senses.definitionCN: 对某物有强烈渴望，通常与 for 连用
senses.example: Fresh from school, she was thirsty for real work.
senses.exampleCN: 刚出校门的她渴望真正的工作。
senses.why: The dry throat becomes the picture of any hunger of the mind: what the body feels for water, the soul feels for its goals.
senses.whyCN: 干渴的喉咙成为一切精神饥饿的图景：身体之于水，正如灵魂之于目标。

senses.title: Dry land or climate
senses.definition: (of land, plants, or weather) dry and needing water
senses.definitionCN: 指土地、植物或气候干燥缺水
senses.example: The thirsty field cracked under the August sun.
senses.exampleCN: 八月的烈日下，干渴的田地裂了缝。
senses.why: The word climbs out of the throat and into the landscape: earth that cannot drink is described with the body's word.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从喉咙爬进风景：喝不上水的土地，用身体的词来描述。

senses.title: Causing thirst
senses.definition: causing thirst, as in hard physical work or a hot task
senses.definitionCN: 引起口渴的，如重体力劳动或炎热的工作
senses.example: Digging the well was thirsty work.
senses.exampleCN: 挖井是件让人口渴的活儿。
senses.why: English turns the feeling around: work that makes you thirsty can itself be called thirsty.
senses.whyCN: 英语把这感觉掉了个头：让人口渴的活儿，本身也可以被称作口渴的。

intro.en: Thirsty is the adjective of thirst, and thirst is a native Germanic word for the burning dryness of the throat, cousin to words for scorched land in the old languages.
intro.cn: thirsty 是 thirst 的形容词；thirst 是日耳曼本土词，指喉咙灼人的干渴，在古语言中与表示焦土的词是亲戚。

items.en: The root Thurstu, generally reconstructed, meant dryness and the craving it causes, related to a root for scorched or dried up.
items.cn: 公认词根一般重构为 Thurstu，意为干渴及其引发的渴求，与表示「烧焦、晒干」的词根相关。

items.en: Old English Thurst (or Thurst) was the noun thirst, and Thurstig (or Thyrstig) the adjective thirsty.
items.cn: 古英语 Thurst (or Thurst) 是名词「渴」，Thurstig (or Thyrstig) 是形容词「渴的」。

items.en: Norse Thyrstr reinforced the northern forms with the same burning picture.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 Thyrstr 以同样的灼烧图景支持了北方形式。

items.en: Middle English thirst and thirsty spread into moral and religious writing, where thirst for righteousness became a standing image.
items.cn: 中古英语 thirst 与 thirsty 进入道德与宗教写作，「渴慕正义」成为固定意象。

items.en: Modern English kept thirsty for body, mind and land alike, and the compound bloodthirsty pushed the metaphor into darker ground.
items.cn: 现代英语让 thirsty 同时服务于身体、心灵与土地，复合词 bloodthirsty 则把比喻推向更暗处。

note.en: The first group holds the thirst family; the second compares the words of wanting and dryness.
note.cn: 第一组是 thirst 词族；第二组比较表示渴求与干燥的词。

entries.definition: the feeling of needing drink, or a strong desire
entries.definitionCN: 渴；口渴；强烈欲望（thirsty 的名词）

entries.definition: the number after twelve; begins with the same thir- sounds but counts, not dries
entries.definitionCN: 十三；开头读音与 thirsty 相近，但表数目不表干渴

entries.definition: the number thirty; shares the first syllable sound with thirsty
entries.definitionCN: 三十；与 thirsty 首音节同音

entries.definition: without water; describes the mouth or the land instead of the feeling
entries.definitionCN: 干的；描述嘴或土地的状态而非感受

entries.definition: keen and impatient for something
entries.definitionCN: 热切的；thirsty for 的近义但无干渴意象

entries.definition: extremely dry, as land or a throat after heat
entries.definitionCN: 焦干的；酷热后土地或喉咙的极干状态

normalIntro.en: Real hooks: the scorched-earth root, the thirst-thirsty pair, and the thirst for image.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：「焦土」词根、thirst-thirsty 对、以及 thirst for 意象。

normal.en: Thirst is the feeling; thirsty is the throat that has it.
normal.cn: thirst 是感觉，thirsty 是有着这感觉的喉咙。

normal.en: Thirsty work: the job makes you thirsty, so it borrows your word.
normal.cn: thirsty work：活儿让你口渴，便借用了你的词。

normal.en: Thirsty for knowledge: the mind has a throat too.
normal.cn: thirsty for knowledge：头脑也有一副喉咙。

normal.en: Bloodthirsty pushes the dryness into cruelty.
normal.cn: bloodthirsty 把干渴推向残忍。

normal.en: Parched is drier than thirsty: the crack comes before the word.
normal.cn: parched 比 thirsty 更干：裂缝先于词语。

abstract.en: Thirsty is the body holding up an empty cup.
abstract.cn: thirsty 是身体举着一只空杯。

abstract.en: Desire learned its grammar from the throat.
abstract.cn: 欲望的语法是从喉咙学来的。

abstract.en: A thirsty field and a thirsty reader crack the same way.
abstract.cn: 干渴的田地与干渴的读者以同样的方式开裂。

examples.en: I always feel thirsty after salty food.
examples.cn: 吃完咸的我总会口渴。

examples.en: The students were thirsty for news of the exam.
examples.cn: 学生们迫切想听到考试的消息。

examples.en: Harvesting in July is thirsty work.
examples.cn: 七月的收割是让人口渴的活儿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑟斯提」——渴得连「瑟」都「提」不动了,先喝口水 → thirsty 口渴的

root: 日耳曼本土词：词根一般重构为 Thurstu「焦干、灼渴」→ 古英语 Thurst「渴」+ 形容词后缀 -ig → thirsty；与古诺斯语 Thyrstr 同源，与「烧焦」词根相关。

sensesIntro.en: Thirsty starts as the dry throat, becomes the hunger of the mind for a goal, the cracked field, and finally work that makes you drink.
sensesIntro.cn: thirsty 始于干渴的喉咙，化为头脑对目标的饥饿、开裂的田地，最终指代那些让人想喝水的活儿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty cup held up by a dry throat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一副干渴的喉咙举着一只空杯。

branches.en: The body asking for water.
branches.cn: 身体讨水喝。

branches.en: The mind asking for its goal.
branches.cn: 头脑索要它的目标。

branches.en: The earth asking for rain.
branches.cn: 大地求雨。

branches.en: The task that empties your throat.
branches.cn: 掏空你喉咙的活儿。

branches.en: Both share one grammar: wanting with the whole body.
branches.cn: 两者共用同一语法：以整个身体去渴望。

intro.en: Thirsty shows the common English path noun plus y: the feeling becomes a quality you can grade.
intro.cn: thirsty 展示了英语常见的「名词加 y」路径：感觉变成可分级的性质。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source; the family is native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语来源；词族为日耳曼本土，拉丁词条留空。

items.meaning: the need for drink; strong desire
items.example: A glass of water killed his thirst.
Thirsty runners found the water stop.
items.exampleCN: 口渴的跑者找到了补水站。

items.example: The longer walk made them thirstier.
He drank thirstily from the stream.
A windy day on the coast.

items.meaningCN: 解渴；熄灭（固定搭配动词）
items.exampleCN: 什么也平息不了她的好奇。

definition_zh: 体贴的；考虑周到的；沉思的；有思想的
definition_en: showing care for other people’s needs, or given to quiet and serious thinking
core_image: 一个人先在心里替你走一遍路，再把伞递到你手上
scene: 下雨的清晨，室友没说话，只在门口多放了一把伞和一张便条。It was thoughtful of her to leave an umbrella by the door on such a wet morning.
sceneCN: 这里 thoughtful 是「体贴的、考虑周到的」（第 1 个义项：替他人着想并付诸行动）；句意为她在这样的雨天把伞放在门口，真是体贴。

derivatives.zh: 由 think 不规则变化而来的名词，义为「想法；思考」，是 thoughtful 的词基
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「体贴地；沉思地」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「体贴；周到；深思」
由否定前缀 un- 加本词构成，义为「不体贴的；考虑不周的」

senses.title: Considerate of other people
senses.definition: showing that you think about other people’s feelings and needs and act to help
senses.definitionCN: 表现出替他人的感受与需要着想，并付诸行动
senses.example: It was thoughtful of him to call before dropping by.
senses.exampleCN: 他来访前先打了个电话，真是体贴。
senses.why: Thought plus the suffix -ful turns the inner act of thinking outward, into care for someone else.
senses.whyCN: thought 加上后缀 -ful，把内心的思考转向外部，变成对他人的照顾。

senses.title: Showing careful thought
senses.definition: carefully planned or considered, so that nothing important is forgotten
senses.definitionCN: 经过仔细计划或考虑，重要之处都没有遗漏
senses.example: The report offers a thoughtful analysis of the housing problem.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告对住房问题做了考虑周到的分析。
senses.why: The same fullness of thought is applied to a piece of work rather than to a person.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「思虑充盈」被用到一件作品上，而不是一个人身上。

senses.title: Quietly absorbed in thought
senses.definition: looking serious and quiet because you are thinking about something
senses.definitionCN: 因在思考某事而显得严肃、安静
senses.example: She sat by the window with a thoughtful expression.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐在窗边，一副若有所思的神情。
senses.why: This is the literal picture: a person whose face shows that the mind is full of thought.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的画面：脸上显出内心塞满思绪的人。

senses.title: Having serious ideas
senses.definition: showing serious and original ideas, of a person, book or film
senses.definitionCN: 指人、书或影片呈现出严肃而有独到见解的思想
senses.example: He is a thoughtful writer who asks uncomfortable questions.
senses.exampleCN: 他是一位有思想的作家，总提让人不适的问题。
senses.why: A mind that is always full of thought is valued for the quality of what it holds.
senses.whyCN: 总是装满意绪的心灵，因其所装之物的分量而受到重视。

intro.en: Thoughtful is a native English compound: the noun thought plus the full-suffix -ful.
intro.cn: thoughtful 是英语本土复合词：名词 thought 加表示「充满」的后缀 -ful。

items.en: The root behind think meant to seem or to appear to the mind, a sense still visible in an old legal phrase.
items.cn: think 背后的词根意为「在心中显现」，这一含义还残留在古老的固定说法里。

items.en: Old English had the verb for thinking and the noun for a thought, built on an old nominal form.
items.cn: 古英语已有表示「思考」的动词与表示「想法」的名词，建立在古老的名词形式上。

items.en: The adjective formed with -ful of thought appears in the Middle English period, first in the sense of being deep in thought.
items.cn: 由 thought 加 -ful 构成的形容词出现于中古英语时期，最初义为「陷入深思的」。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the word had moved outward: thoughtful came to mean considerate of other people.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，这个词向外转：thoughtful 开始表示「替他人着想的」。

items.en: Modern use keeps both directions side by side, the inner thinker and the outward kindness.
items.cn: 现代用法让两个方向并存：内心的思考者与向外的善意。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on thought; the second compares words of consideration and thinking.
note.cn: 第一组收以 thought 为词基的一族词；第二组比较表示体贴与思考的词。

entries.definition: The noun for an idea or the act of thinking, also the past of think.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「想法；思考」，也是 think 的过去式

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning in a considerate or meditative way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「体贴地；沉思地」

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being considerate or deep in thought.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「体贴、周到、深思」

entries.definition: Grateful; it rhymes with thoughtful and uses the same suffix but another base, so the root differs.
entries.definitionCN: 感激的；与本词押韵且后缀相同，但词基不同，词源不同

entries.definition: Careful not to trouble or hurt others; the closest formal partner of thoughtful.
entries.definitionCN: 体贴的；为他人着想的（最接近的正式近义词）

entries.definition: Paying close attention to someone and their needs.
entries.definitionCN: 殷勤的；关注他人需要的

entries.definition: Showing love and concern for others, warmer and more emotional.
entries.definitionCN: 关心人的（更温暖、更多情感色彩）

entries.definition: Quietly thinking, often with a hint of sadness.
entries.definitionCN: 沉思的（带一丝忧愁，文学色彩）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the base noun, the suffix -ful, and the outward turn the word took.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自词基名词、后缀 -ful，以及这个词后来向外的转向。

normal.en: Thoughtful is thought plus -ful: a head full of thought, aimed at someone else.
normal.cn: thoughtful 就是 thought 加 -ful：满脑子思绪，只是朝着别人的方向。

normal.en: A thoughtful gift shows that someone thought about you before choosing it.
normal.cn: 贴心的礼物说明有人先想到你，才去挑选。

normal.en: A thoughtful silence is a thinking silence, not an angry one.
normal.cn: thoughtful silence 是思考的静默，不是生气的静默。

normal.en: The adverb is thoughtfully, the noun thoughtfulness.
normal.cn: 副词是 thoughtfully，名词是 thoughtfulness。

normal.en: Do not mix it with thankful: one is care, the other is gratitude.
normal.cn: 不要与 thankful 相混：一个是体贴，一个是感激。

abstract.en: Picture someone walking your day in their head before it happens, then leaving what you will need.
abstract.cn: 想象有人在心里先把你的一天走一遍，然后把你需要的东西留下。

abstract.en: Thought is water; the suffix -ful makes it a cup filled to the brim, offered to someone.
abstract.cn: 思绪是水，后缀 -ful 让它成为满满一杯，端给别人。

abstract.en: The word points both inward to the quiet thinker and outward to the quiet helper.
abstract.cn: 这个词既指向内心的默想者，也指向安静的帮忙者。

examples.en: It was thoughtful of you to remember my birthday.
examples.cn: 你还记得我的生日，真是体贴。

examples.en: She gave the plan a thoughtful review before agreeing.
examples.cn: 她在同意前对这个计划做了周密的审视。

examples.en: He grew thoughtful whenever the name was mentioned.
examples.cn: 一提到那个名字，他就陷入沉思。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「梭特福」——心里来回穿梭,把福气先留给别人 → thoughtful 体贴的

root: 英语本土复合：thought（think 的不规则名词形，源自古英语表示「思考」的词）+ 后缀 -ful「充满……的」；最初指「陷入深思」，十八世纪起扩展为「替他人着想的」。

sensesIntro.en: Thoughtful fills the head with thought and then points it in two directions: outward to other people and their needs, inward to a quiet thinking mind.
sensesIntro.cn: thoughtful 让头脑装满思绪，再把这份思绪指向两个方向：向外给他人的需要，向内给安静的思考者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: walking someone else’s day inside your head, then leaving what they will need.
core.cn: 核心意象：在心里先替别人走一遍他的一天，再留下他会需要的东西。

branches.en: The person: thought turned into kindness for others.
branches.cn: 人线：思绪转化为对他人的善意。

branches.en: The work: the same fullness of thought spent on a report or a plan.
branches.cn: 作品线：同样的思虑充沛被用在报告或计划上。

branches.en: The face: the literal picture of a mind at work.
branches.cn: 面容线：心灵运转时最字面的画面。

branches.en: The writer: thoughts valuable enough to be a reputation.
branches.cn: 作者线：思绪深到足以成为一种名声。

branches.en: Inner and outer halves of the same suffixed word.
branches.cn: 同一个带后缀词的向内与向外两半。

intro.en: Thoughtful is built natively with the suffix -ful, and English adds -ly and -ness on top.
intro.cn: thoughtful 由本土后缀 -ful 构成，英语再在其上叠加 -ly 与 -ness。

latinIntro.en: The base and suffix are both English, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 词基与后缀都属英语，拉丁词条留空。

items.meaning: an idea; the act of thinking

items.example: We are thankful for your help.
A considerate host checks the heating.
items.exampleCN: 体贴的主人会查看暖气。

definition_zh: 威胁；恐吓；危及；预示凶险
definition_en: to say that you will harm someone, to put someone or something in danger, or to seem about to do something bad
core_image: 天边推过来一整片乌云，压得人抬不起头
scene: 堤坝上的水位一夜涨了三尺,守夜人不停往村里打电话。The rising flood threatened the whole village.
sceneCN: 这里 threaten 是「危及、威胁到」（第 2 个义项：使某事处于危险中）；句意为上涨的洪水危及整个村庄。

collocations.zh: 威胁要做某事；眼看就要……

derivatives.zh: 由动词去掉后缀 -en 得到的名词，义为「威胁；危险」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「威胁的；凶险的」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「受到威胁的；濒危的」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「威胁地」

senses.title: To say you will harm someone
senses.definition: to tell someone that you will hurt them or cause trouble unless they do what you want
senses.definitionCN: 告诉对方若不听命就会伤害他或制造麻烦
senses.example: The caller threatened to publish the photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 打电话的人威胁说要公布那些照片。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an act: pressure is applied out loud, before any blow.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：压力在拳头落下之前就大喊着施加出来。

senses.title: To put in danger
senses.definition: to be likely to harm someone or something, of a thing rather than a person
senses.definitionCN: 指事物而非人可能造成伤害
senses.example: Smoke from the factory threatens the health of nearby residents.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂排出的烟危及附近居民的健康。
senses.why: Pressure need not come from a voice; a flood or a policy presses in just as hard.
senses.whyCN: 压力不必来自声音；洪水或政策压得同样沉。

senses.title: To seem about to happen
senses.definition: to look as if something bad is going to happen, of clouds, events or a situation
senses.definitionCN: 指乌云、事件或局势看起来即将发生坏事
senses.example: Dark clouds threatened rain all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 整个下午乌云都预示着一场雨。
senses.why: The verb lets an inanimate thing lean forward: the sky itself seems to be pressing.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词让无生命之物也前倾身体：连天空看起来都在施压。

senses.title: To endanger an institution or system
senses.definition: to put the continued existence of an organisation, system or custom at risk
senses.definitionCN: 使组织、制度或习俗的存续面临风险
senses.example: The cuts threaten the future of the local library.
senses.exampleCN: 这些削减让本地图书馆的未来岌岌可危。
senses.why: Once anything can press, the passive follows easily: a library, a language or a job can be threatened.
senses.whyCN: 一旦任何事物都能施压，被动式便顺理成章：图书馆、语言或工作都能处于威胁之下。

intro.en: Threaten is the verb made from the noun threat with the Germanic suffix -en, which also makes widen and strengthen.
intro.cn: threaten 是由名词 threat 加日耳曼语后缀 -en 构成的动词，widen、strengthen 也是同样的做法。

items.en: The old root meant to press or crowd, the pressure behind both threat and throng.
items.cn: 古老词根意为「压、挤」，威胁与 throng 背后的压迫感同源。

items.en: Old English had a verb of the same shape meaning to press or force, alongside the noun for a crowd and for compulsion.
items.cn: 古英语已有同形动词表示「压迫、胁迫」，与表示人群和强制的名词并存。

items.en: Middle English rebuilt the verb on the noun with -en, and threaten came to mean uttering harm or showing danger.
items.cn: 中古英语以名词为词基加 -en 重造动词，threaten 遂表示「扬言伤害」或「显露危险」。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the verb extended to things: clouds, storms and diseases could threaten.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，这个动词扩展到事物：乌云、风暴与疾病都能 threaten。

items.en: Modern English uses the passive freely, so a species can be threatened with extinction.
items.cn: 现代英语大量使用被动式，于是可以说某个物种面临灭绝的威胁。

note.en: The first group gathers the threat family; the second compares verbs of menacing and warning.
note.cn: 第一组收 threat 词族；第二组比较表示威胁与警告的动词。

entries.definition: The noun, a warning of harm or a source of danger.
The adjective for a menacing look, letter or sky.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「威胁的、凶险的」

entries.definition: The adjective for something put at risk, as in an endangered species.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「受到威胁的、濒危的」

entries.definition: To make strong, built with the same -en ending but another base, so the root differs.
entries.definitionCN: 加强；与本词同为 -en 动词，但词基不同，词源不同

entries.definition: To be a threat to someone, often of a person or mood.
To frighten someone into doing what you want.
entries.definitionCN: 恐吓；胁迫（使人因害怕而服从）

entries.definition: To put someone or something in danger, with no suggestion of words.
entries.definitionCN: 危及（不含言语威胁之意）

entries.definition: To tell someone about a possible danger so they can avoid it.
entries.definitionCN: 警告（出于提醒，而非施压）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the -en verb pattern, the two main uses, and the passive form.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自 -en 动词规律、两种主要用法，以及被动式。

normal.en: Threaten is threat plus -en, the same way strength becomes strengthen.
normal.cn: threaten 就是 threat 加 -en，正如 strength 变成 strengthen。

normal.en: People threaten and things threaten: one with words, the other with pressure.
normal.cn: 人会威胁，物也会威胁：一个用言语，一个用压力。

normal.en: Threaten to rain is the sky making a promise it may not keep.
normal.cn: threaten to rain 是天空许下的一个未必兑现的承诺。

normal.en: Be threatened with closure means a job or a place is on the line.
normal.cn: be threatened with closure 意为一份工作或一个地方岌岌可危。

normal.en: The noun is threat; remember the verb carries the extra -en.
normal.cn: 名词是 threat；记住动词多带了 -en。

abstract.en: Picture a storm front pushing across the sky, pressing the whole town down before a drop falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一道雨锋推过天空，一滴雨未落就把整座城压住。

abstract.en: To threaten is to lean forward without stepping.
abstract.cn: threaten 是身体前倾，却不迈出那一步。

abstract.en: The verb gives danger a voice and a body: words at the door, water at the wall.
abstract.cn: 这个动词给危险一副嗓音和一具身体：门口的话语，墙外的水。

examples.en: The two firms threatened each other with lawsuits.
examples.cn: 两家公司互相威胁要打官司。

examples.en: Rising seas threaten these coastal farms.
examples.cn: 海面上升危及这些沿海农场。

examples.en: It threatened to snow all morning but never did.
examples.cn: 整个上午都像要下雪，却始终没下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死瑞腾」——死命拽着不放，逼得人腾不出身 → threaten 威胁

root: 名词 threat（日耳曼词根「压、挤」）加动词后缀 -en 构成，与 widen、strengthen 同型；由「出声施压」扩展为「以事物之势危及」，并衍生被动式「面临……威胁」。

sensesIntro.en: Threaten applies pressure in three voices: a person speaking harm, a force putting something at risk, and a sky that hints at what is coming.
sensesIntro.cn: threaten 以三种嗓音施加压力：人说出伤害、力量使某物处于险境、天空暗示即将来临之事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a storm front pressing across the sky before a single drop falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴雨未落就压过天空的雨锋。

branches.en: The voice: harm named out loud as leverage.
branches.cn: 嗓音线：把伤害说出口当作筹码。

branches.en: The force: smoke, water or heat doing the pressing.
branches.cn: 力量线：烟、水或热在施压。

branches.en: The sky: clouds that hint and never quite deliver.
branches.cn: 天空线：乌云暗示着，却往往落空。

branches.en: The institution: a library or a custom on the line.
branches.cn: 机构线：图书馆或习俗岌岌可危。

branches.en: Passive forms let anything be threatened, from health to a species.
branches.cn: 被动式让任何对象都能被威胁，从健康到物种。

intro.en: Threaten is a noun turned verb by -en, and the family adds -ing, -ed and -ly.
intro.cn: threaten 是由名词加 -en 转成的动词，词族再叠加 -ing、-ed 与 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Both the base and the suffix are native Germanic, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 词基与后缀都属日耳曼本土，拉丁词条留空。

definition_zh: 兴旺；繁荣；茁壮成长；蓬勃发展
definition_en: to grow well and be healthy, or to be successful and continue growing strongly
core_image: 窗台上一盆绿植越过花盆边缘，越窜越高
scene: 小区角落原本光秃的墙根,如今爬山虎长得密密匝匝。The old brick wall is now covered with ivy that thrives in the damp shade.
sceneCN: 这里 thrive 是「茁壮成长」（第 2 个义项：植物长得旺盛）；句意为那面旧砖墙如今爬满了在潮湿阴处长得旺盛的常春藤。

collocations.zh: 在压力下反而表现出色

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「兴旺的；繁荣的」
本词的过去分词形式，义为「已兴旺起来」
与本词同源的近亲名词，义为「节俭」（语义已分化）

senses.title: To succeed and grow strong
senses.definition: to become successful, strong and healthy, of a business, city or person
senses.definitionCN: 指事业、城市或人变得成功、强健、健康
senses.example: The little bookshop thrived after it began hosting readings.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小书店开始办朗读会之后兴旺起来。
senses.why: The Norse verb meant to take a firm hold, so success is pictured as a grip that holds.
senses.whyCN: 这个北欧语动词意为「牢牢抓住」，因此成功被想象成一把抓稳的手。

senses.title: To grow vigorously, of plants
senses.definition: to grow strongly and healthily, especially of plants in favourable conditions
senses.definitionCN: 尤指植物在适宜条件下长得健壮旺盛
senses.example: These roses thrive in full sun and well-drained soil.
senses.exampleCN: 这些玫瑰在阳光充足、排水良好的土里长得很好。
senses.why: Applied to plants, the grip image becomes roots holding soil and shoots pushing up.
senses.whyCN: 用在植物上，抓握的意象就变成根系抓住土壤、枝条向上推送。

senses.title: To do well in difficult conditions
senses.definition: to do well because of conditions that would weaken others, used with on or under
senses.definitionCN: 因那些会削弱别人的条件而表现得更好，后接 on 或 under
senses.example: Some people thrive on a tight deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 有些人在紧迫的期限下反而状态极好。
senses.why: The preposition on marks the source: the pressure itself feeds the growth.
senses.whyCN: 介词 on 标出源头：压力本身成了生长的养分。

senses.title: To flourish culturally or socially
senses.definition: to develop strongly and spread, of ideas, arts or customs
senses.definitionCN: 指观念、艺术或习俗发展壮大并传播开来
senses.example: Coffee culture thrives in this part of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡文化在城市的这一带很盛行。
senses.why: Ideas are treated like plants: they take hold, spread and bloom across a place.
senses.whyCN: 观念被当作植物看待：它们落地、蔓延，在一个地方成片开花。

intro.en: Thrive comes from Old Norse, and its older meaning was to grasp or to seize, not to grow.
intro.cn: thrive 来自古北欧语，较早的意义是「抓住」，并非「成长」。

items.en: The Norse verb þrífask meant to prosper and also to grasp or take hold of something.
items.cn: 北欧语动词 þrífask 既表示「兴旺」，也表示「抓住、握住」。

items.en: The root behind it meant to grip or to press, the same pressure family that gives threat.
items.cn: 其背后的词根意为「抓紧、压住」，与 threat 同属压迫一族。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word from Norse settlers and used it for growing strong and prospering.
items.cn: 中古英语从北欧移民借入这个词，用来表示「长得强健」与「兴旺」。

items.en: Early modern English gave the word both a bodily and a commercial sense, a thriving plant and a thriving trade.
items.cn: 早期现代英语让它兼具身体与商业两面：茁壮的植物与兴隆的生意。

items.en: Modern English added the pattern thrive on, meaning to do better because of something.
items.cn: 现代英语发展出 thrive on 的用法，表示「因某事而更好」。

note.en: The first group gathers the thrive family and its Norse relatives; the second compares words of success and growth.
note.cn: 第一组收 thrive 词族及其北欧近亲；第二组比较表示成功与生长的词。

entries.definition: The adjective for a healthy, growing business or plant.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「兴旺的、繁荣的」

entries.definition: From the same Norse family, meaning careful management of money.
entries.definitionCN: 节俭（同源，语义已转向理财）

entries.definition: The adjective of thrift, meaning careful with money.
Very exciting; the -ill- pattern is close but the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 令人激动的（-ill- 拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: To grow or develop very well, especially of plants and arts.
entries.definitionCN: 繁荣；茂盛（尤指植物与艺术）

entries.definition: To become successful, usually of money and business.
entries.definitionCN: 兴旺；致富（多指经济层面）

entries.definition: To open into flower, and figuratively to come into your own.
To dry up and fade, the exact opposite of thriving.

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the Norse origin, the grip image, and the thrive on pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自北欧来源、「抓握」意象，以及 thrive on 句式。

normal.en: The old Norse verb meant to grab hold, and a plant that thrives has taken firm hold of its soil.
normal.cn: 古北欧语动词意为「抓住」，长得旺的植物正是抓住了土。

normal.en: Thrive on shows the pattern: the thing that would hurt others helps you.
normal.cn: thrive on 显示这种句式：会让别人受伤的东西反而帮了你。

normal.en: The past tense form throve is old style, and thrived is the everyday choice.
normal.cn: 过去式 throve 偏古，日常多用 thrived。

normal.en: Thrift comes from the same Norse family: both words are about making something go far.
normal.cn: thrift 出自同一条北欧语脉：两个词都关乎「让有限之物发挥到极致」。

normal.en: A thriving market and a thriving rose bush share one word.
normal.cn: 繁荣的市场与旺盛的玫瑰丛共用一个词。

abstract.en: Picture a vine that has found the one crack of light and climbed over the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一株藤找到了唯一的裂缝阳光，一路爬过墙头。

abstract.en: To thrive is not just to survive the winter but to burst out in spring.
abstract.cn: thrive 不只是熬过冬天，而是春天炸开般地生长。

abstract.en: The word makes growth look like a grip that keeps getting tighter.
abstract.cn: 这个词让成长看起来像一把越握越紧的手。

examples.en: Small firms thrive when rules are simple.
examples.cn: 规则简单时，小公司就能兴旺。

examples.en: These plants thrive in damp, shaded corners.
examples.cn: 这些植物在阴湿的角落里长得很好。

examples.en: She thrives on difficult problems.
examples.cn: 她越遇到难题越有劲头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踹五」——一脚踹开五道门槛，生意越踹越旺 → thrive 兴旺

root: 古北欧语 þrífask「兴旺；抓住」，与日耳曼语「抓紧、压住」词根同源（与 threat 同族）；中古英语借入后表示「长壮、兴旺」，现代又发展出 thrive on 的用法。

sensesIntro.en: Thrive keeps one image of taking a firm hold and lets it grow into business success, healthy plants, strength under pressure and living cultures.
sensesIntro.cn: thrive 保留「牢牢抓住」这一个意象，让它蔓生为事业成功、植物健壮、压力下的强韧与兴盛的文化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vine that has found the light and climbed over the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：找到阳光、一路爬过墙头的藤。

branches.en: The venture: businesses and people doing well.
branches.cn: 事业线：生意与人越来越好。

branches.en: The plant: roots that grip and shoots that climb.
branches.cn: 植物线：根系紧抓，枝条上扬。

branches.en: The strain: doing better exactly where others fail.
branches.cn: 压力线：恰在别人撑不住处表现出色。

branches.en: The culture: ideas and habits spreading and blooming.
branches.cn: 文化线：观念与习惯传播开来、开花结果。

branches.en: Commercial and botanical growth share one word.
branches.cn: 商业增长与植物生长共用一个词。

intro.en: Thrive stays simple; English adds -ing and the older irregular endings.
intro.cn: thrive 保持简单，英语在其上加 -ing 以及较老的不规则词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word comes through Old Norse with no Latin source, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 本词经古北欧语而来，没有拉丁语来源，拉丁词条留空。

definition_zh: 遍及；贯穿整个；自始至终
definition_en: in every part of a place or thing, or during the whole of a period of time
core_image: 一盏灯从屋顶照下来，屋里每个角落都被照亮
scene: 这座城市从南到北都在下雨,骑车的人个个罩着雨衣。Rain fell throughout the city, from the harbour to the northern hills.
sceneCN: 这里 throughout 是「遍及、贯穿整个」（第 1 个义项：空间上的每一处）；句意为整座城市从港口到北边山地都在下雨。

forms.label: 无变化（介词与副词同形）

derivatives.zh: 复合中的前一部分，义为「穿过」
复合中的后一部分，义为「向外、全部」
同根孪生词，义为「彻底的」

senses.title: In every part of a place
senses.definition: in or into every part of a place, area or object
senses.definitionCN: 在某地、某区域或某物体的每一部分中
senses.example: The fire alarm could be heard throughout the building.
senses.exampleCN: 整栋楼都能听见火警铃声。
senses.why: Through supplies the passage and out supplies the spread, so the word covers every part of a space.
senses.whyCN: through 提供「贯穿」，out 提供「铺开」，于是这个词覆盖了一个空间的每一部分。

senses.title: During the whole of a period
senses.titleCN: 自始至终；贯穿整个时期
senses.definition: during the whole of a period of time, from beginning to end
senses.definitionCN: 在某段时间的整个过程中，从头到尾
senses.example: She remained calm throughout the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 整个面试过程中她都保持镇定。
senses.why: Time is crossed the same way a space is: the compound reaches both ends of the period.
senses.whyCN: 时间与空间以同样的方式被穿过：这个复合词抵达这段时间的两端。

senses.title: In all parts of a group or field
senses.definition: in every part of a group, field or body of work
senses.definitionCN: 在某个群体、领域或全部作品中的每一处
senses.example: The idea appears throughout his early novels.
senses.exampleCN: 这个想法贯穿他早期的小说。
senses.why: A body of work is treated like a place, and the idea is found in every part of it.
senses.whyCN: 一批作品被当作一个地方，而这个想法在其中每一处都能找到。

senses.title: As a standalone adverb
senses.definition: used alone, especially after a noun, to mean in every part or the whole time
senses.definitionCN: 单独作副词，尤用于名词之后，表示「处处」或「一直」
senses.example: The house was painted white throughout.
senses.exampleCN: 这所房子里里外外都刷成了白色。
senses.why: With no noun after it, the compound simply means all over, in space or in time.
senses.whyCN: 后面不接名词时，这个复合词就单纯表示「到处、始终」，用于空间或时间。

intro.en: Throughout is a plain English compound of through and out, first recorded in the Old English period.
intro.cn: throughout 是 through 与 out 构成的朴实英语复合词，最早见于古英语时期。

items.en: The compound of þurh and ūt already meant on every side or entirely, built the same way as other out compounds.
items.cn: þurh 与 ūt 的复合在古英语已表示「四面八方、完全」，与其他带 out 的复合词构词相同。

items.en: Middle English throughout kept both the spatial sense and the temporal one, and settled as a single word.
items.cn: 中古英语 throughout 兼有空间与时间两义，并固定为一个词。

items.en: Early modern English added the extended use for groups and works, as in throughout his writings.
items.cn: 早期现代英语增添了用于群体与作品的引申用法，如 throughout his writings。

items.en: Modern English uses throughout more in writing than in speech, where all through is often preferred.
items.cn: 现代英语里 throughout 多用于书面，口语更常用 all through。

items.en: The adverb use without a following noun remains common, as in painted white throughout.
items.cn: 不接名词的副词用法依然常见，如 painted white throughout。

note.en: The first group unpacks the compound and its relatives; the second compares prepositions of extent.
note.cn: 第一组拆解这个复合词及其亲属；第二组比较表示范围的介词。

entries.definition: From one side to the other; the first half of the compound.
The everyday spoken equivalent, common before a period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 口语常用说法，多接时间段

entries.definition: Complete and careful; the adjective twin of through.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底的（through 的形容词孪生词）

entries.definition: Covering every part of a place; the loose spoken partner of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 遍布；本词的口语松散对应说法

entries.definition: In every place; it cannot take a noun after it.
Covering the whole of a surface or place, often informally.
From one side to the other, or over the whole of an area.
Through the course of a period; it does not mean everywhere in a place.
entries.definitionCN: 在……期间（不含空间「遍及」义）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the two parts of the compound and from its written register.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自复合词的两个部分，以及它的书面语体。

normal.en: Throughout is through plus out: passing through, then spread out everywhere.
normal.cn: throughout 就是 through 加 out：先穿过，再铺开到各处。

normal.en: Use it for places and for periods, but not for a point in time.
normal.cn: 它用于地点与时段，不用于某个时间点。

normal.en: In speech, all through often does the same job.
normal.cn: 口语里 all through 常干同样的活。

normal.en: The adverb use takes no noun: white throughout means white all over.
normal.cn: 副词用法不接名词：white throughout 意为里外全白。

normal.en: Mind the noun after it: throughout the city, not throughout city.
normal.cn: 注意后面要有冠词或限定词：throughout the city。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp hung from the ceiling, reaching the corners the floor lamp misses.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏吊灯挂在天花板上，照到了落地灯照不到的角落。

abstract.en: The word stretches a space or a period until nothing outside it remains.
abstract.cn: 这个词把一个空间或一段时间拉长，直到外面什么都不剩。

abstract.en: It is the quiet, written cousin of everywhere.
abstract.cn: 它是 everywhere 那个安静的书面对应词。

examples.en: The festival is celebrated throughout the country.
examples.cn: 这个节日在全国各地都庆祝。

examples.en: He kept notes throughout the lecture.
examples.cn: 整场讲座他都在记笔记。

examples.en: The walls were painted pale grey throughout.
examples.cn: 墙里里外外都刷成了浅灰色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「出路熬特」——出路熬到特别久，一路贯彻到底 → throughout 自始至终

root: 古英语由 þurh（through，穿过）+ ūt（out，向外）复合而成，表示「四面八方、完全」，后兼指时间自始至终，并引申用于群体与作品。

sensesIntro.en: Throughout stretches the tunnel image over a space, a period, a body of work, or the whole of an object.
sensesIntro.cn: throughout 把隧道意象拉伸到一片空间、一段时间、一批作品，或一个物体的整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp hung high, lighting every corner at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：高悬的灯，一次照亮每个角落。

branches.en: The space: every room, every region.
branches.cn: 空间线：每间屋、每个地区。

branches.en: The period: from beginning to end.
branches.cn: 时段线：从开头到结尾。

branches.en: The field: across a whole body of ideas or novels.
branches.cn: 领域线：贯穿全部想法或小说。

branches.en: The object: white throughout, without a noun.
branches.cn: 物体线：white throughout，不带名词。

branches.en: Place and time are stretched by the same compound.
branches.cn: 空间与时间由同一个复合词拉满。

intro.en: Throughout is itself a compound; it does not take further endings.
intro.cn: throughout 本身已是复合词，不再加其他词尾。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are native English, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都是英语本土词，拉丁词条留空。

definition_zh: 雷；雷声；轰隆声；怒吼
definition_en: the loud noise that follows lightning in a storm, or any very loud rolling sound
core_image: 乌云压顶，一道白光之后整片天空轰隆隆地滚过
scene: 夏夜的雨来得急,雷声在孩子头顶滚过,他一下子钻进被子里。The thunder rolled across the valley and the child hid under the blanket.
sceneCN: 这里 thunder 是「雷声」（第 1 个义项：雷雨中紧随闪电的巨大声响）；句意为雷声滚过山谷，孩子躲进了被子里。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ous 构成，义为「雷鸣般的；轰响的」
由 thunder 与 storm 复合，义为「雷暴」
由 thunder 与 bolt 复合，义为「霹雳；雷电」
由本词加 -y 构成，义为「有雷的；闷热欲雷的」

senses.title: The noise after lightning
senses.definition: the loud rolling noise heard after a flash of lightning during a storm
senses.definitionCN: 雷雨中闪电之后听到的巨大滚响
senses.example: A clap of thunder woke the whole house.
senses.exampleCN: 一声炸雷惊醒了整幢房子。
senses.why: Thor, the hammer-wielding god of storms, hides in the first syllable of this word.
senses.whyCN: 手持锤子的雷神托尔（Thor）就藏在这个词的第一个音节里。

senses.title: Any loud rolling sound
senses.definition: a very loud, deep and continuing noise made by traffic, water, applause or a crowd
senses.definitionCN: 车辆、水流、掌声或人群发出的响亮而低沉的连续声响
senses.example: The thunder of the waterfall could be heard a mile away.
senses.exampleCN: 瀑布的轰鸣声一英里外就能听到。
senses.why: Any sound as deep and continuous as a storm borrows the storm’s name.
senses.whyCN: 凡是像风暴那样低沉而持续的声音，都可以借用风暴的名字。

senses.title: To make a loud rolling noise
senses.definition: to make a loud deep noise, or for the sky to sound with thunder
senses.definitionCN: 发出响亮低沉的声响，或指天上打雷
senses.example: The trucks thundered past on the old bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车在老桥上一路轰隆而过。
senses.why: The verb keeps the physical roar: heavy things moving with a rolling noise.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留实体的轰鸣：沉重之物带着滚动之声前进。

senses.title: To shout angrily
senses.definition: to speak very loudly and angrily, often of a person in authority
senses.definitionCN: 大声而愤怒地说话，多指有权威的人
senses.example: The coach thundered at the players to get back in line.
senses.exampleCN: 教练对球员怒吼，叫他们排好队。
senses.why: A human voice raised to storm volume takes the same word.
senses.whyCN: 人声抬到风暴的音量，就用同一个词。

intro.en: Thunder is named after Thor, the Germanic god of storms, and the word has kept his hammer in its sound.
intro.cn: thunder 取自日耳曼雷神 Thor 之名，读音里还留着那把锤子的分量。

items.en: The common Germanic word for the storm god was Thunraz, borrowed as Thor in Norse and Thunor in Old English.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中雷神之名为 Thunraz，北欧语作 Thor，古英语作 Thunor。

items.en: Old English þunor was both the god and the noise he was thought to make, so the natural sound and the god shared one name.
items.cn: 古英语 þunor 既是神，也是人们认为神发出的响声，自然之声与神共用一个名字。

items.en: When the speaker d moved into the word, the spelling thunder fixed the modern form and the god faded from it.
items.cn: 插入了 d 音之后，拼写 thunder 固定下来，神的身影也跟着隐去。

items.en: Modern English extends thunder to engines, crowds and waterfalls, and the verb to angry speech.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到引擎、人群与瀑布，动词则扩用于愤怒的说话。

items.en: Idioms such as steal someone’s thunder still remember a storm that can be taken away.
items.cn: steal someone’s thunder 一类习语，仍记得那场可以被夺走的风暴。

note.en: The first group gathers the thunder family and near spellings; the second compares loud natural sounds.
note.cn: 第一组收 thunder 词族与形近词；第二组比较自然界的大声响。

entries.definition: The adjective, as in thunderous applause.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，如「雷鸣般的掌声」

entries.definition: A storm with thunder and lightning.
A flash of lightning with a crash, and a sudden shock.
Beneath something; it hides inside thunder but has a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 在……下面（藏在 thunder 之中，词源不同）

entries.definition: The flash of electricity in a storm; it comes before the thunder.
entries.definitionCN: 闪电（雷雨中的电光，先于雷声）

entries.definition: A low continuous sound, often further away and weaker than thunder.
A very loud deep sound made by a lion, crowd, engine or sea.
entries.definitionCN: 咆哮；轰鸣（多由狮、人群、引擎或海发出）

entries.definition: A short deep explosive sound, like a drum.
entries.definitionCN: 低沉的爆响（短促，如鼓声）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the god Thor, the silent-looking d and the storms the word names.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自雷神 Thor、看起来「多出来」的 d，以及它命名的各种风暴。

normal.en: Thor is the thunder god, and his name is the first four letters.
normal.cn: Thor 是雷神，他的名字就是这个词的前四个字母。

normal.en: The d was added by speakers, so thunder sounds nothing like its spelling suggests.
normal.cn: 这个 d 是口语里后加的，读音与拼写差得很远。

normal.en: Thunder follows lightning; the light comes first and the sound arrives later.
normal.cn: thunder 跟在 lightning 之后：先见光，后闻声。

normal.en: Thunderous applause has nothing to do with storms but the volume.
normal.cn: 雷鸣般的掌声与风暴无关，只是音量相似。

normal.en: Steal someone’s thunder means to take the credit before they can speak.
normal.cn: steal someone’s thunder 意为抢在别人开口前抢走功劳。

abstract.en: Picture a whole sky rolling over like a heavy barrel down a stone road.
abstract.cn: 想象整片天空像一只重桶在石路上滚过。

abstract.en: The same word names the weather, applause and an angry voice.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既命名天气，也命名掌声与怒声。

abstract.en: Thunder is the sound of something enormous happening out of sight.
abstract.cn: thunder 是某件巨大之事在视野之外发生时的响动。

examples.en: Thunder rolled over the hills all evening.
examples.cn: 整个傍晚雷声都在山间滚动。

examples.en: The audience gave the singer thunderous applause.
examples.cn: 观众给歌手送上了雷鸣般的掌声。

examples.en: The waves thundered against the harbour wall.
examples.cn: 海浪轰隆隆地拍打着港口墙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「散得」——满天闷响一时散得干干净净 → thunder 雷声

root: 古英语 þunor，源自日耳曼雷神之名 Thunraz（北欧语 Thor），一词兼指雷神与其轰鸣；中古英语插入 d 音定型为 thunder，后引申为一切轰响与怒吼。

sensesIntro.en: Thunder begins as the voice of the storm god and spreads to every deep, rolling noise, from engines to angry coaches.
sensesIntro.cn: thunder 起初是雷神的声音，后来扩散到一切低沉滚动的巨响，从引擎到怒吼的教练。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole sky rolling over like a barrel on stone.
core.cn: 核心意象：整片天空像桶滚石路一般碾压而过。

branches.en: The weather: a storm’s deep voice.
branches.cn: 天气线：风暴的低沉嗓音。

branches.en: The world: waterfalls, lorries and applause.
branches.cn: 世界线：瀑布、卡车与掌声。

branches.en: The action: a sky or engine that thunders.
branches.cn: 动作线：天空或引擎在轰响。

branches.en: The voice: authority raised into a roar.
branches.cn: 人声线：权威抬高成咆哮。

branches.en: Storm and machinery borrow each other’s volume.
branches.cn: 风暴与机械互相借用彼此的音量。

intro.en: Thunder takes -ous and -y, and compounds with storm and bolt.
intro.cn: thunder 可加 -ous、-y，并与 storm、bolt 复合。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, though -ous and -y are borrowed endings that English applies freely.
latinIntro.cn: 词干为日耳曼语，-ous 与 -y 是英语借入后自由使用的后缀。

items.meaning: a lightning flash with a crash

definition_zh: 雷暴；产生雷电的对流天气；强雷暴；比喻喧闹的风波
definition_en: a convective storm that produces thunder and lightning, usually with heavy rain and sometimes hail or strong wind
core_image: 平原上竖起一座高耸的云塔，云底翻卷发黑，云中不断亮起又熄灭的电光
scene: 平原的闷热午后，云底开始旋转下压，远处传来第一声闷响。A thunderstorm built a dark, rotating base above the fields.
sceneCN: 这里指「产生雷电的对流性天气系统」（第 1 个义项：云中电荷分离并放电的雷暴）；句意为雷暴在田野上方筑起旋转的暗色云底。图中可辨识物件：高耸的云塔、翻卷的云底、云中的电光、被压暗的田地。

pos.zh: 雷暴；雷暴雨；喧闹的风波

derivatives.zh: 有雷的；闷雷似的
雷鸣般的；轰隆作响的
雷云
雷暴云砧顶
霹雳；雷电

senses.title: A storm that produces thunder and lightning
senses.titleCN: 产生雷电的对流性风暴
senses.definition: a convective storm that produces thunder and lightning, usually with heavy rain
senses.definitionCN: 产生雷电、通常伴有强降水的对流性风暴
senses.example: A thunderstorm built a dark, rotating base above the fields.
senses.exampleCN: 雷暴在田野上方筑起旋转的暗色云底。
senses.why: Thunder plus storm: the compound names a storm defined by the sound and light it makes, not by rainfall alone.
senses.whyCN: 由雷与风暴复合而成：这个词以声音和电光来定义风暴，而不只看降水量。

senses.title: A convective cell in meteorology
senses.definition: an organised updraft cell in which warm moist air rises, cools and releases latent heat
senses.definitionCN: 暖湿空气上升、冷却并释放潜热的有组织上升气流单体
senses.example: Doppler radar showed a single thunderstorm cell growing over the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 多普勒雷达显示有一个雷暴单体在山脊上发展。
senses.why: Forecasters use the word for the unit of convection itself, because that unit is what a radar can follow.
senses.whyCN: 预报员用这个词指对流的基本单元，因为雷达追踪的正是这个单元。

senses.title: A short-lived single-cell storm
senses.titleCN: 生命史短暂的单单体雷暴
senses.definition: a brief single-cell storm whose updraft and downdraft share one column and die within an hour
senses.definitionCN: 上升与下沉气流共用同一气柱、通常一小时内消散的短时单单体风暴
senses.example: The afternoon thunderstorm lasted barely forty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这场午后雷暴只持续了不到四十分钟。
senses.why: The single-cell type is the simplest case: one column rises, rains itself out and collapses.
senses.whyCN: 单单体是最简单的情形：一根气柱上升、把自己下成雨，然后坍塌。

senses.title: A multicell or supercell system
senses.titleCN: 多单体或超级单体雷暴系统
senses.definition: a larger storm in which several cells line up, or one rotating updraft persists for hours
senses.definitionCN: 多个单体排列成线、或单一旋转上升气流持续数小时的更大风暴
senses.example: A supercell thunderstorm kept its rotating updraft for three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 一个超级单体雷暴维持旋转上升气流达三小时。
senses.why: Once cells share a common inflow, the storm stops behaving like a single brief column.
senses.whyCN: 当多个单体共享同一入流，风暴就不再像一根短暂的气柱了。

senses.title: A severe thunderstorm
senses.titleCN: 达到强雷暴标准的雷暴
senses.definition: a thunderstorm that meets severity criteria such as large hail, damaging wind or a tornado
senses.definitionCN: 达到大冰雹、破坏性大风或龙卷等强度标准的雷暴
senses.example: The warning was issued because the thunderstorm carried hail the size of golf balls.
senses.exampleCN: 之所以发布警报，是因为这场雷暴带着高尔夫球大小的冰雹。
senses.why: Severity is a legal and operational threshold, not a poetic judgement, so the word gains a fixed technical edge.
senses.whyCN: 「强」是业务与法规上的阈值，而非文学判断，因此这个词获得了固定的技术边界。

senses.title: A dry thunderstorm
senses.definition: a thunderstorm whose rain evaporates before reaching the ground, leaving only lightning and wind
senses.definitionCN: 雨水在落地前蒸发、只留下闪电与强风的雷暴
senses.example: A dry thunderstorm started three fires on the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 一场干雷暴在山脊上引发了三次火情。
senses.why: When the rain never arrives, lightning becomes the whole story, which is why fire services watch this type closely.
senses.whyCN: 当雨始终落不下来，闪电就成了全部内容，因此消防部门格外关注这一类。

senses.title: A thunderstorm day in climate records
senses.definition: a day on which thunder is heard at a station, counted as a climate statistic
senses.definitionCN: 观测站听到雷声的一天，作为气候统计计入
senses.example: The station averages thirty thunderstorm days a year.
senses.exampleCN: 该站平均每年有三十个雷暴日。
senses.why: Climatology needs a countable unit, so it counts days with thunder rather than individual cells.
senses.whyCN: 气候学需要一个可计数的单位，于是统计听到雷声的日子，而非单个单体。

senses.title: A noisy uproar, metaphorically
senses.definition: a loud, chaotic outburst of criticism or conflict likened to a storm
senses.definitionCN: 被比作雷暴的、喧闹混乱的批评或冲突爆发
senses.example: The proposal set off a thunderstorm of criticism in the press.
senses.exampleCN: 该提案在媒体上引发了一场批评的雷暴。
senses.why: The compound gives metaphor a louder and more sudden image than plain storm, which is why it suits public uproar.
senses.whyCN: 比起单说风暴，这个复合词提供更响、更突然的意象，因此适合形容公共喧闹。

intro.en: Thunderstorm is an English compound of two native words, thunder and storm. It is recorded from the seventeenth century, once the compound was needed to name a storm defined by thunder and lightning. No Latin element enters the word.
intro.cn: thunderstorm 是由两个本族词雷与风暴构成的英语复合词，17 世纪起有记录，当时需要用这个复合词来指以雷电为特征的storm。该词不含拉丁语素。

items.en: Thunder goes back to Old English thunor and storm to Old English storm; both elements are Germanic and were already common weather words.
items.cn: thunder 可溯至古英语 thunor，storm 可溯至古英语 storm；两个成分都属日耳曼语，且早已是常用天气词。

items.en: The joined form thunderstorm appears in English writing in the seventeenth century as a plain descriptive compound.
items.cn: 合并形式 thunderstorm 在 17 世纪出现在英语书面语中，是一个直白的描述性复合词。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century meteorology narrowed the word to a convective cell with lightning, and later to classified types.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪的气象学把该词收窄为带闪电的对流单体，随后又分出类型。

items.en: Modern forecasting separates single-cell, multicell and supercell thunderstorms according to how their updrafts are organised.
items.cn: 现代预报按上升气流的组织方式，把雷暴分为单单体、多单体与超级单体。

items.en: A severe thunderstorm is defined by hail, damaging wind or a tornado rather than by rainfall, a twentieth-century operational standard.
items.cn: 强雷暴以冰雹、破坏性大风或龙卷来界定，而不以降水量界定，这是 20 世纪的业务标准。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): dictionary dates for the first use of the compound differ by several decades, and no single citation is treated as authoritative; the word's formation itself is not in doubt.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：各词典给出的复合词首见年代相差数十年，没有单一书证被视为权威；但该词的构成方式本身并无疑义。

note.en: Group one holds the two source words and the cloud-part term most often mistaken for the whole storm; group two holds neighbouring convective terms.
note.cn: 第一组是两个来源词，以及最容易被误当作整个雷暴的云体部位名；第二组是相近的对流术语。

entries.definition: The second element alone: any violent wind storm, with or without lightning.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词的后半单独使用：任何剧烈风暴，有雷电与否均可。

entries.definition: The first element alone: the sound of the discharge, with no rain and no storm implied.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词的前半单独使用：只指放电发出的声音，不含降雨或风暴。

entries.definition: The towering upper part of a cumulonimbus, not the storm as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 积雨云高耸的上部，而不是整个雷暴。

entries.definition: A long line of convective cells that moves as one front; it may contain many thunderstorms.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一条锋面整体移动的长条对流单体带，其中可含多个雷暴。

entries.definition: A rotating thunderstorm with a persistent mesocyclone; the name is a subtype, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 具有持续中气旋的旋转雷暴；该名称是下位类型，并非同义词。

entries.definition: A storm named for the hail it drops, which may or may not be a thunderstorm.
entries.definitionCN: 以落下的冰雹命名的风暴，它未必是雷暴。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real source words, the real classification and the real operational threshold.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的来源词、真实的分型与真实的业务标准。

normal.en: Thunder plus storm: the storm is named by the sound it makes.
normal.cn: 雷加风暴：这场风暴以它发出的声音命名。

normal.en: Three types by updraft: single cell, multicell, supercell.
normal.cn: 按上升气流分三类：单单体、多单体、超级单体。

normal.en: Severe means hail, damaging wind or a tornado, not heavy rain.
normal.cn: 「强」指冰雹、破坏性大风或龙卷，而不是大雨。

normal.en: Climate counts thunderstorm days, not individual cells.
normal.cn: 气候统计计雷暴日，而不计单个单体。

normal.en: A dry thunderstorm drops lightning without rain reaching the ground.
normal.cn: 干雷暴只落下闪电，雨水到不了地面。

abstract.en: Picture a chimney that builds itself, rains inside itself and then collapses.
abstract.cn: 想象一根自己长出来、在自己内部下雨、随后坍塌的烟囱。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd whose shouting is so loud that it sounds like weather.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人的喊声大到听起来像天气。

abstract.en: Picture a fire started by a storm that brought no water.
abstract.cn: 想象一场没带水来的风暴点着了火。

examples.en: The pilot diverted around a line of thunderstorms over the plains.
examples.cn: 飞行员绕开了平原上空的一列雷暴。

examples.en: Severe thunderstorm warnings are issued when hail or damaging wind is expected.
examples.cn: 预计出现冰雹或破坏性大风时，会发布强雷暴警报。

examples.en: The station logs a thunderstorm day whenever thunder is heard.
examples.cn: 只要听到雷声，该站就记一个雷暴日。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「thunder（雷）+ storm（风暴）」——打雷下雨的风暴 → 雷暴

root: 英语本族复合词：thunder（古英语 thunor，原始日耳曼 *thunraz）+ storm（古英语 storm，原始日耳曼 *sturmaz）。不含拉丁语素，latinEntries 留空。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the plain weather event to its technical cell, its classified types, its severity threshold, its climate count and finally its use as a metaphor for uproar.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从日常天气现象，依次走到技术上的对流单体、分类类型、强度阈值、气候计数，最后用作喧闹风波之喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tower of cloud that carries its own engine, its own light and its own collapse.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座自带发动机、自带电光、也自带坍塌的云塔。

branches.en: THE EVENT AND ITS UNIT: the everyday storm and the radar cell are the same object at two scales.
branches.cn: 事件与其单元：日常所说的雷暴与雷达追踪的单体，是同一对象在两种尺度上。

branches.en: ORGANISATION: one column dies fast; many cells or one rotating updraft last for hours.
branches.cn: 组织方式：单根气柱很快消散；多单体或单一旋转上升气流能维持数小时。

branches.en: THRESHOLD: severity is fixed by hail, wind or tornado, not by rain.
branches.cn: 阈值：强度由冰雹、大风或龙卷界定，而不是由雨界定。

branches.en: NO RAIN: when precipitation evaporates aloft, lightning stands alone.
branches.cn: 无雨：当降水在高空蒸发，闪电便独自登场。

branches.en: COUNT AND METAPHOR: climate turns it into days, rhetoric turns it into noise.
branches.cn: 计数与比喻：气候学把它变成天数，修辞把它变成喧闹。

intro.en: Thunderstorm is a transparent English compound, so its parts and its combining patterns can be read directly.
intro.cn: thunderstorm 是一个透明的英语复合词，其成分与复合模式可以直接读出。

latinIntro.en: Both elements are Germanic weather words; no Latin prefix or root takes part in the compound.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都是日耳曼语天气词，复合过程中没有拉丁前缀或词根参与。

items.example: A thundery afternoon kept the climbers low.
items.exampleCN: 一个有雷的午后让登山者留在低处。

items.example: The hall broke into thunderous applause.
items.exampleCN: 大厅里爆发出雷鸣般的掌声。

items.meaning: the anvil top of a cumulonimbus
items.example: The thunderhead spread across the horizon.
items.exampleCN: 雷暴云砧在地平线上铺开。

items.meaning: one convective unit of a storm
items.example: Radar followed the cell for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 雷达追踪该单体达一小时。

items.meaning: an official alert for severe storms
items.meaningCN: 针对强雷暴的官方警报

items.meaning: a day on which thunder is heard
items.example: The map plots thunderstorm days per year.
items.exampleCN: 该图绘出每年的雷暴日数。

definition_zh: 票；入场券；罚单；（政党）候选人名单
definition_en: a piece of paper or a digital pass that gives you the right to travel, enter or attend something
core_image: 一张印着几行小字的小纸片，检票口看一眼就放行
scene: 出门赶车前他忽然在口袋里翻找,怕那张小纸片弄丢了。She checked her pocket twice to make sure the ticket was still there.
sceneCN: 这里 ticket 是「车票」（第 1 个义项：凭以乘车的小票据）；句意为她摸了两次口袋，确认车票还在。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「售票；开罚单」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「持票的；被开罚单的」
由 ticket 与 holder 复合，义为「持票人」

senses.title: A pass for travel or entry
senses.definition: a printed or digital piece of evidence giving the holder the right to travel or enter
senses.definitionCN: 纸质或电子凭证，持者有乘车或入场的权利
senses.example: Two return tickets to the city, please.
senses.exampleCN: 请给我两张到城里的往返票。
senses.why: The word began as a written note, and a note is enough to pass a gate.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是一张书面便条，而一张便条足以通过一道闸。

senses.title: A notice of a fine
senses.definition: an official notice that you must pay a fine for a traffic or parking offence
senses.definitionCN: 因交通或停车违章而须缴纳罚款的正式通知
senses.example: There was a parking ticket under the windscreen wiper.
senses.exampleCN: 雨刷下夹着一张违章停车罚单。
senses.why: The right to pass became a right to punish: the same slip of paper, in another colour.
senses.whyCN: 「准予通行」变成了「予以处罚」：同一张小纸片，换了个颜色。

senses.title: A means to an end
senses.definition: in phrases such as a ticket to success, the thing that enables you to reach a goal
senses.definitionCN: 用于 a ticket to success 一类短语，指使人达到目标的手段
senses.example: Fluent English was her ticket to a better job.
senses.exampleCN: 流利的英语是她得到更好工作的门径。
senses.why: Whatever lets you through a door is a ticket, even when it is not paper.
senses.whyCN: 凡是能让你通过一道门的东西都是 ticket，即使它不是纸。

senses.title: A political list of candidates
senses.definition: the list of candidates that a party puts forward in an election
senses.definitionCN: 政党在选举中推出的候选人名单
senses.example: He won a place on the party ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 他赢得了该党名单上的一个位置。
senses.why: Candidates travel on one list as passengers travel on one ticket.
senses.whyCN: 候选人同上一个名单，就像乘客凭同一张票同行。

intro.en: Ticket came into English from French, where it began as a short note rather than a travel pass.
intro.cn: ticket 经法语进入英语，最初指一张短小的便条，而非车票。

items.en: Old French estiquet meant a note or a label, something stuck onto a document or a door.
items.cn: 古法语 estiquet 意为便条或标签，是贴在文书或门上的东西。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word as ticket, and it named a written note, a licence or a short record.
items.cn: 中古英语借入作 ticket，指书面便条、许可证或简短记录。

items.en: By the seventeenth century ticket had become the slip that admits you to a coach, a play or a lottery draw.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，ticket 已指让人乘车、看戏或抽签的凭据。

items.en: The nineteenth century added the police sense, the ticket that charges rather than admits.
items.cn: 十九世纪增添了警察用法：不再放行而是处罚的票单。

items.en: Modern English made tickets digital, but the word still means the right to go through.
items.cn: 现代英语让票数字化了，但这个词仍表示「可以过去」的权利。

note.en: The first group separates ticket from near spellings; the second compares passes, vouchers and fines.
note.cn: 第一组区分 ticket 与形近词；第二组比较票证、凭单与罚款。

entries.definition: A check mark, or a small insect; one syllable less and another root.
entries.definitionCN: 勾；蜱虫（少一个音节，词源不同）

entries.definition: To touch lightly and make someone laugh.
The rise and fall of the sea; a different root entirely.
An adhesive label, literally a thing stuck on.
entries.definitionCN: 贴纸（同源，本义「贴上去的东西」）

entries.definition: A card or document that lets you enter freely, often repeatedly.
A printed piece of paper exchangeable for goods or money.
The money paid for a journey, not the paper itself.
Money paid as a penalty; the ticket is only the notice of it.
entries.definitionCN: 罚款（票只是通知，钱才是罚）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the short-note origin and the two opposite jobs of the same slip.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自「便条」的来源，以及同一纸片两种相反的职责。

normal.en: Ticket began as a little note, and a note still gets you through a gate.
normal.cn: ticket 最初是一张小便条，而一张便条仍能让你过闸。

normal.en: A travel ticket lets you go; a parking ticket stops you with a fine.
normal.cn: 车票放你过去，罚单则用罚款拦住你。

normal.en: Ticket office is where you pay before, the ticket machine where you pay quickly.
normal.cn: ticket office 是提前买票的地方，ticket machine 是快速买票的机器。

normal.en: A ticket to success is not paper; it is whatever opens the door.
normal.cn: 通往成功的 ticket 不是纸，而是任何能开门的凭据。

normal.en: Do not mix it with tick or tide: check the middle letters.
normal.cn: 不要与 tick 或 tide 混：看清中间的字母。

abstract.en: Picture a small slip flicked across a counter, the one thing that decides whether you pass.
abstract.cn: 想象一张小纸片从柜台那头弹过来，它单单决定你能不能过去。

abstract.en: The word is a legal token: it carries permission in miniature.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一枚微型的法律凭证，把许可装在小尺寸里。

abstract.en: The same paper can open a door or close a bank account.
abstract.cn: 同一张纸可以打开一扇门，也可以掏空一个账户。

examples.en: I booked two tickets for the evening train.
examples.cn: 我订了两张晚班火车的票。

examples.en: He got a ticket for parking on the pavement.
examples.cn: 他因为人行道上停车被开了罚单。

examples.en: Good writing is still a ticket to better work.
examples.cn: 好文笔仍是通往更好工作的门径。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「替课特」——替人上课特批一张凭条 → ticket 票

root: 古法语 estiquet「便条、标签」，中古英语借入为 ticket，本指书面便条或许可；十七世纪转指乘车看戏的凭据，十九世纪又衍生出交警罚单义。

sensesIntro.en: Ticket is a small slip that carries permission, and the same shape of paper can also carry a penalty, a career chance or a party list.
sensesIntro.cn: ticket 是一张承载许可的小纸片，同一形状的纸也能承载罚款、职业机会或政党名单。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small slip flicked across a counter that decides whether you pass.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张从柜台弹来的小纸片，决定你能不能过去。

branches.en: The pass: permission in miniature.
branches.cn: 通行线：微缩的许可。

branches.en: The fine: the same slip turned against you.
branches.cn: 罚款线：同一纸片反过来对付你。

branches.en: The chance: whatever opens a door.
branches.cn: 机会线：任何能开门的凭据。

branches.en: The list: candidates travelling together on one ballot.
branches.cn: 名单线：候选人共用一张选票同行。

branches.en: Two opposite powers share one small piece of paper.
branches.cn: 两种相反的权力共住一张小纸片。

intro.en: Ticket takes -s, -ed and -ing; it compounds with office, holder and machine.
intro.cn: ticket 可加 -s、-ed、-ing，并与 office、holder、machine 复合。

latinIntro.en: The stem came through French from an old root for sticking, with no Latin entry needed here.
latinIntro.cn: 词干经法语而来，源出表示「粘贴」的古老词根，此处无需拉丁词条。

definition_zh: 潮汐的；与潮汐有关的；受潮水涨落支配的
definition_en: relating to the tide, the regular rise and fall of sea level caused by the gravitational pull of the moon and the sun
core_image: 海水沿着同一道岸坡一天两次爬上来，又顺着同一个坡退回去，像有人在极慢地呼吸
scene: 沿海公路旁，测量员把潮汐表摊在引擎盖上，对照岸边的刻度说，Records of tidal water levels from this bay go back two centuries.
sceneCN: 这里 tidal 指「与潮汐这一自然现象有关的」（第 1 个义项：潮汐的、潮汐观测的）；句意为：这个海湾的潮位记录可以追溯到两百年前。

pos.zh: 受潮水涨落支配的；随潮汐节律的（多作定语，比较级罕用）

forms.label: 比较级（关系形容词，罕用）
最高级（关系形容词，罕用）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成：以潮汐的方式；随潮汐节律地
由「潮」加「陆地」构成的复合词：受潮水淹没的滩地
由「潮」加「线」构成的复合词：高潮退去后留下的杂物线、潮线
由「潮」加「水」构成的复合词：受潮水推动的水；潮水灌溉的低地
由「潮」加「闸门」构成的复合词：挡潮闸，退潮时放水、涨潮时挡住海水

senses.title: Of the tide as a phenomenon
senses.definition: relating to the tide as a physical phenomenon, including its timing, its height and the study of it
senses.definitionCN: 与潮汐这一物理现象有关的，包括其时刻、高度以及相关研究
senses.example: Records of tidal water levels from this bay go back two centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个海湾的潮位记录可以追溯到两百年前。
senses.why: tide began as a word for 'time', and -al means 'of or belonging to'; tidal therefore says 'of the tide' before it narrows to any particular place.
senses.whyCN: tide 最初是「时间」之词，-al 表示「属于……的」；因此 tidal 首先只是「潮汐的」，之后才收窄到具体场合。

senses.title: A place the tide governs
senses.definition: of a harbour, bay or stretch of shore that is open to the tide and whose water level changes with it
senses.definitionCN: 指敞开迎潮、水位随潮水升降的港口、海湾或河岸
senses.example: The harbour is tidal, so boats leave before the water drops.
senses.exampleCN: 这个港口受潮水支配，所以船只要在水位退下前离港。
senses.why: a place described by what controls it takes the relational adjective; a tidal harbour is one where the tide, not the harbour, sets the water level.
senses.whyCN: 用支配它的力量来描写一个地点时就用这个关系形容词；受潮港口的意思是潮水而非港口本身决定水位。

senses.title: Driven by the tide
senses.definition: using the rise and fall of the tide as a source of motion or electric power
senses.definitionCN: 把潮水的涨落当作动力或电力来源的
senses.example: A tidal scheme could light the island twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 一套潮汐发电方案能一天两次为这座岛供电。
senses.why: the adjective of origin also marks the source of power: what belongs to the tide can be turned into what runs on the tide.
senses.whyCN: 这个表示来源的形容词也能标出动力来源：属于潮汐的东西，可以被改造成靠潮汐运转的东西。

senses.title: Of the intertidal strip
senses.definition: of the zone between the high and low water marks, covered at high tide and bare at low tide
senses.definitionCN: 指高水位线与低水位线之间、涨潮被淹、退潮露出的地带
senses.example: Crabs wait out the low water in tidal pools.
senses.exampleCN: 螃蟹在潮池里熬过退潮的那段时间。
senses.why: that strip has no everyday name of its own, so the adjective does the work: it is the part of the shore the tide owns.
senses.whyCN: 那条地带在日常生活里没有专门名称，于是由形容词承担：它是岸上归潮水所有的那一段。

senses.title: Reversing with the tide
senses.definition: of a current or stream whose direction turns with the flood and the ebb
senses.definitionCN: 指方向随涨潮与退潮而反转的水流
senses.example: Pilots time their entry to a favourable tidal stream.
senses.exampleCN: 引航员会掐着顺向的潮流水势进港。
senses.why: a stream that turns is 'of the tide' in direction as well as in schedule, and the adjective covers both at once.
senses.whyCN: 会掉头的水流在方向上和时间上都「属于潮汐」，一个形容词同时覆盖这两层。

senses.title: Keeping tidal time
senses.definition: of a rhythm in a living thing that is set by the tide rather than by daylight
senses.definitionCN: 指生物体内由潮汐而非日照设定的节律
senses.example: Shorebirds feed on a tidal clock rather than on the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 滨鸟按潮汐的钟点觅食，而不是按太阳的钟点。
senses.why: biology needed a word for clocks the moon winds, and the existing adjective supplied it without any new coinage.
senses.whyCN: 生物学需要为「月亮上弦的钟」找一个词，现成的形容词直接顶上，不必再造新词。

senses.title: Reached by the tide upstream
senses.definition: of the lower course of a river that salt water enters and pushes back twice a day
senses.definitionCN: 指海水每天两次灌入并顶托的河流下游段
senses.example: The lower river is tidal as far as the weir.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河的下游一直到拦河堰都是感潮的。
senses.why: the tide does not stop at the coast; where it forces its way up a river, that reach becomes literally of the tide.
senses.whyCN: 潮水并不止于海岸；它顶进河流的那一段，字面上就成了「潮汐的」地盘。

senses.title: Of a gravitational tide
senses.definition: of the bulge or force raised in one body by another body's gravity, with or without water
senses.definitionCN: 指一个天体被另一个天体的引力拉出的隆起或作用力，无论表面有没有水
senses.example: The moon lifts a tidal bulge in the solid rock.
senses.exampleCN: 月球在坚硬的岩层里也拉起一个潮汐隆起。
senses.why: physics kept the water image and moved it to rock: what the moon raises in the earth is of the same nature as the sea's tide.
senses.whyCN: 物理学保留水的意象又把它挪到岩石上：月球在地球里拉出的隆起，与海潮在性质上相同。

senses.title: Of one breath's volume
senses.definition: of the volume of air moved in or out in a single ordinary breath
senses.definitionCN: 指一次平静呼吸进出肺部的空气体积
senses.example: The nurse recorded the patient's tidal volume every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 护士每小时记录一次病人的潮气量。
senses.why: breathing repeats like the water's rise and fall, so respiratory physiology borrowed the adjective for the air moved in one cycle.
senses.whyCN: 呼吸像水的涨落一样往复，呼吸生理学于是借这个形容词，指一个周期里进出的空气量。

intro.en: Tidal is a native Germanic noun fitted with a borrowed suffix: Old English tīd 'time' became tide, and English added -al to make an adjective from it. The word is recorded in tide-related writing from the eighteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tidal 是一个日耳曼本族名词加外来后缀的构造：古英语 tīd「时间」演变为 tide，英语再加 -al 构成形容词。这个词从 18 世纪的潮汐类写作中开始见于书证，年代均为约数。

items.en: Tīd meant 'time, hour, season, appointed time' and survives in eventide and Yuletide; the Germanic noun behind it is reconstructed as *tīdiz, the same word as German Zeit, so the sea sense grew out of the fixed hours at which high water was expected.
items.cn: tīd 意为「时间、时辰、季节、约定的时刻」，今仍存于若干表示时令的旧词中；其背后的日耳曼名词重构为 *tīdiz，与德语 Zeit 同词，海潮义正是从「高潮到来的固定时刻」长出来的。

items.en: By the fourteenth century tide named the rise and fall of the sea itself, and high tide and low tide had become fixed phrases.
items.cn: 到 14 世纪，tide 已指海水本身的涨落，「高潮」与「低潮」成为固定说法。

items.en: The adjective suffix -al goes back to Latin -alis by way of Norman French; English attaches it freely to nouns (tidal, coastal, legal) to mean 'of or belonging to'.
items.cn: 形容词后缀 -al 经诺曼法语上溯到拉丁 -alis；英语把它自由地加在名词后，表示「属于……的」。

items.en: Tidal appears in eighteenth-century writing on harbours and tide tables, where an adjective was needed for the phenomenon itself rather than for a particular tide.
items.cn: tidal 见于 18 世纪关于港口与潮汐表的写作，当时需要一个形容词来指这一现象本身，而不是某一次具体的潮。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the adjective spread to tidal power, tidal force in astronomy and tidal volume in physiology, each time keeping the core relation 'of the tide'.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪，这个形容词扩展到潮汐发电、天文学中的引潮力、生理学中的潮气量，每次都保留「属于潮汐」这一核心关系。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only, not root): the earliest citation of tidal is generally placed in the eighteenth century but is not precisely dated; *tīdiz is a reconstruction, while the cognacy of tide and German Zeit is not in doubt.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代，不涉及词根）：tidal 的最早书证一般定在 18 世纪，但没有确切年份；*tīdiz 是重构形式，而 tide 与德语 Zeit 同源这一点并无争议。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like tidal or are built on the same stem, including two that end alike but come from different roots; group two holds words used about the same coastal setting.
note.cn: 第一组是与 tidal 形近或同出同一词干的词，其中两个结尾相同但词根不同；第二组是用于同一海岸情境的词。

entries.definition: the rise and fall of the sea itself; tidal only describes what belongs to it, so the noun cannot stand in for the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 海水本身的涨落；tidal 只描写属于它的东西，因此这个名词不能替代形容词。

entries.definition: tidal plus -ly, describing how something is done or driven, as in a tidally flushed lagoon.
entries.definitionCN: tidal 加 -ly，描写某事以何种方式发生或被驱动，如「靠潮水冲刷的潟湖」。

entries.definition: from Latin titulus 'inscription, label'; the shared ending is accidental and there is no tide in it.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 titulus「铭文、标签」；相同的词尾纯属巧合，与潮汐无关。

entries.definition: from bride plus -al, meaning 'of a wedding'; it rhymes with tidal but is built on a different noun.
entries.definitionCN: 由「新娘」一词加 -al 构成，意为「婚礼的」；它与 tidal 押韵，却建立在另一个名词上。

entries.definition: between the high and low water marks; it names one zone, while tidal can qualify anything connected with the tide.
entries.definitionCN: 位于高低潮线之间；它只指一个地带，而 tidal 可修饰任何与潮汐有关的事物。

entries.definition: of the shore, whether or not tides reach it; it is a wider term than tidal.
entries.definitionCN: 海岸的，无论潮水是否到达；它比 tidal 范围更宽。

entries.definition: of an estuary, the place where a river meets the tide; it names the setting rather than the tide's influence.
entries.definitionCN: 河口湾的，即河流与潮水相遇之处；它指这类地点，而非潮汐的影响。

entries.definition: recurring at regular intervals; tidal behaviour is one kind of periodic behaviour, so the general word is wider.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定间隔重复的；潮汐行为是周期性行为的一种，因此这个一般词的范围更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English tīd meant 'time', and the tide keeps its own clock: high water arrives at fixed hours.
normal.cn: 古英语 tīd 意为「时间」，潮水也自带时钟：高潮总在固定的时刻到来。

normal.en: The family runs tide, tidal, tidally, tideland, tideline, tidewater, tidegate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 tide、tidal、tidally、tideland、tideline、tidewater、tidegate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the coastal sense: tidal flat, tidal pool, tidal current, tidal bore.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出海岸义：潮滩、潮池、潮流、涌潮。

normal.en: German Zeit 'time' is the cousin of tide; the two words split long before English existed.
normal.cn: 德语 Zeit「时间」是 tide 的表亲，两词在英语形成之前就已分开。

normal.en: A relational adjective rarely takes more or most: the comparative sounds awkward in ordinary use.
normal.cn: 关系形容词很少用比较级：在普通用法里，比较级听起来很别扭。

abstract.en: Picture the sea climbing a stone stair, one step every six hours.
abstract.cn: 想象海水在爬石阶，每六个小时上一级。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hands are moved by the moon instead of by a spring.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟，指针不靠发条，而由月亮推动。

abstract.en: Picture a river that briefly turns salty and flows backwards twice a day.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河一天两次短暂变咸，并倒着流。

examples.en: Tidal water reached the lower streets before dawn.
examples.cn: 天亮前，潮水已经漫到低处的街道。

examples.en: The tidal flat teems with worms and shells at low water.
examples.cn: 退潮时，潮滩上尽是沙蚕与贝壳。

examples.en: Engineers survey tidal currents before anchoring the turbine.
examples.cn: 工程师在固定涡轮之前先勘测潮流。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抬陡」——潮水抬得又陡又快，一转眼漫上滩面 → 潮汐的、受潮水支配的

root: 古英语 tīd「时间、时辰」（日耳曼语重构 *tīdiz，与德语 Zeit 同源）→ 中古英语 tide 兼指海水的定时涨落 → tide + 形容词后缀 -al → tidal；*tīdiz 属构拟形式。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all keep one relation, 'of the tide': the phenomenon and its records, the places it governs, the power drawn from it, the strip it owns, the currents it turns, the clocks it winds, the rivers it pushes up, the rock it bulges, and finally the breath it resembles.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都守着同一个关系「属于潮汐」：现象及其记录、受它支配的地点、从它取用的动力、它拥有的地带、它反转的水流、它上弦的钟、它顶进的河流、它拉起的岩层，最后是它所比拟的一次呼吸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the sea climbing and retreating along the same shore twice a day, on a schedule set by the moon.
core.cn: 核心意象：海水沿着同一道岸坡一天涨落两次，时刻由月亮定下。

branches.en: THE BASIC RELATION: first the phenomenon and its records, then the places and waters it governs.
branches.cn: 基本关系：先是现象及其记录，然后是受它支配的地点与水域。

branches.en: TIDE AS FORCE: the water that spins a turbine is the same water that reverses a channel.
branches.cn: 潮汐作为力：转动涡轮的水，与让水道掉头的水是同一股。

branches.en: THE STRIP THE TIDE OWNS: between the marks, the tide decides what may live and when.
branches.cn: 潮水拥有的地带：在两条水位线之间，潮汐决定谁能生存、何时生存。

branches.en: TIDE AS CLOCK AND AS INTRUSION: organisms keep its rhythm, and rivers feel its push upstream.
branches.cn: 潮汐作为时钟与侵入者：生物守着它的节律，河流感到它向上游的顶托。

branches.en: THE IMAGE EXTENDED: gravity raises rock, and breathing repeats like water.
branches.cn: 意象的延伸：引力拉起岩石，呼吸像水一样往复。

intro.en: Tidal is a native Germanic noun with a borrowed suffix: tide comes from Old English, while -al reached English through Latin and French and then became fully productive.
intro.cn: tidal 是日耳曼本族名词加外来后缀：tide 来自古英语，而 -al 经拉丁语与法语进入英语，随后成为能产后缀。

latinIntro.en: Only the suffix is Latin (-alis); tide itself has no Latin cognate, since it descends from Germanic *tīdiz. The Latin entries are therefore empty by design, and Latin-based look-alikes such as title belong to other roots.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后缀是拉丁的（-alis）；tide 本身来自日耳曼 *tīdiz，没有拉丁同族词，因此拉丁条目按实情留空；像 title 这类拉丁系形近词属于别的词根。

items.example: High water came at the appointed tīd.
items.exampleCN: 高潮在约定的时辰到来。

items.example: The same suffix builds tidal from tide.
items.exampleCN: 同一个后缀把 tide 构成 tidal。

items.meaning: the rise and fall of the sea
of or relating to the tide
in a manner driven by the tide
the line of debris left by high water
items.meaningCN: 高潮退去后留下的杂物线
items.example: A tideline of plastic marked the beach.
items.exampleCN: 一道塑料垃圾的潮线划在海滩上。

items.meaning: water moved by the tide; low coastal land
items.meaningCN: 受潮水推动的水；沿海低地
items.example: Tidewater reaches the old mill pond.
items.exampleCN: 潮水能涨到那座旧磨坊的水塘。

items.meaning: a gate that keeps the tide out
items.example: The tidegate protects the low fields.
items.exampleCN: 挡潮闸保护低处的田地。

items.example: Intertidal rocks are bare at low water.
items.exampleCN: 退潮时潮间带的礁石裸露出来。

definition_zh: 潮；潮汐；潮流；趋势
definition_en: the regular rise and fall of the sea, or a strong tendency in events or opinion
core_image: 海水沿着沙滩一点点爬上来，又悄悄退回去
scene: 退潮后的滩涂上留下一个个小水洼,孩子们踩着水找螃蟹。At low tide the children searched the wet sand for crabs.
sceneCN: 这里 tide 是「潮、潮汐」（第 1 个义项：海水的定期涨落）；句意为退潮时孩子们在湿沙里找螃蟹。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -al 构成，义为「潮汐的；潮水的」
由 tide 与 water 复合，义为「潮水；（美国）滨海地区」
形式相近但词源不同的名词，义为「消息」，勿混

senses.title: The rise and fall of the sea
senses.definition: the regular rise and fall of the sea caused by the pull of the moon and sun
senses.definitionCN: 由日月引力引起的海水定期涨落
senses.example: The tide comes in quickly along this beach.
senses.exampleCN: 这片海滩涨潮很快。
senses.why: The sea sense grew from the phrase tide of the sea, the scheduled time of the water.
senses.whyCN: 海洋义从 tide of the sea 这一说法长出来，指海水按时涨落。

senses.title: A tendency in events or opinion
senses.definition: a strong and changing tendency of events, opinion or fortune
senses.definitionCN: 事件、舆论或运势强烈而正在变化的走向
senses.example: The tide of opinion turned against the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 舆论的潮流转而对这个计划不利。
